text.p: The following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Any student who wins a medal in international science olympiads will automatically be offered direct admission to science and engineering courses at the two universities here.
- Workers' Party election candidate Tang Liang Hong says he left Singapore as he could not take lightly a letter saying it was "God's will" he be given a death sentence.
- Police said they had not received any report from Tang Liang Hong about alleged threats to his life and called on the Workers' Party member to assist in their investigation.
- Singapore's largest department store, Takashimaya, slashed its net loss by slightly more than half to S$16 million last year and aims to achieve a S$43 million net profit next year.
- Retailers chalked up a mere 3.0 percent increase in credit sales to S$801 million in the year ended June 1996 because of a weak retail sector, according to a Department of Statistics paper.

- The Central Provident Fund (CPF) has spelt out new investment guidelines for fund managers of CPF approved unit trusts following revised rules allowing them to invest up to 40 percent in regional stock exchanges from January 1.

- Intel Corporation unveiled first multi-media enhanced version of its dominant Pentium microprocessor, throwing into sharp focus a running debate on whether, and to what extent, super-chip will harm multimedia companies like Singapore's Creative Technology and Aztech Systems.
- Seven months after May curbs, property market's sombre mood has spilled over into prime districts where owners are prepared to sell at or below valuation.

- Malaysian ringgit strengthened further against dollar. After a brief stop at M$2.4950 in morning trading, it spent most of Asian session Wednesday nudging the M2.4900 mark, a level not seen since August 16.

- The High Court threw out an attempt by A.R. Jumabhoy and his son, Iqbal, to wind up Scotts Investments (Singapore), a move which could lead to a change in the balance of power at listed Scotts Holdings Ltd (SHL).
